doc.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Schools today and the Marsalis family
title: The Musicians' Village and the music center
summary: He explains Branford and Harry Connick Jr.'s music center.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: In the village. In the Musicians’ Village.

No, not the center. We went out to the Musicians’ – did we see it? We went out there, but we didn’t see the center. We just saw some of the houses. We’ll get to that, but please finish what you’re saying. I’m going to ask you about your involvement with that, as well.

I’m mostly a consultant. I’m – that’s basically it, because I am not teaching. I may do some teaching, but for the most part, when it finally does open, there’ll be people that are teaching. I might stick my nose in a little bit here and there.
How did you become associated with the center?

Branford and Harry [Connick], Jr., came here and was wading through all that water. When they saw the damage, the two of them started to talk and said, there’s got to be something we can do. So they started to think about establishing a center. The Musicians’ Village was already underway here, because the Habitat had been building houses down there for a long time. The Musicians’ Village was already there. I think that the property came from the school board. I think there was a school there before it. The management, Ann Marie Wilkins, her agency, who is their manager, Branford and Harry, said okay, let’s do it. She’s been raising money, getting funds and all that, to set up an endowment for it. The money to build it had been in the bank for a while. So it’s almost done. In fact I’m surprised you didn’t see it, because if you’re going up there, it’s kind of hard not to see.
I think we did. Maybe it just wasn’t identified, the site.
You went to the Musicians’ – because Brad Pitt is building houses down there too.
Were those the ones you saw?
It wasn’t clear. We had Andrea [? Du Plessis] who took us out there to look at – to see some of the developments out there.
I don’t know. I don’t know if you saw the Musicians’ Village or not.
She identified it as such, but I don’t recall seeing the center.

Maybe it was. Anyway, the building is pretty much close to – maybe not move in, because I think they’re supposed to finish it in the spring. But it’s definitely a community center with an emphasis on music.
